scope: Reviewed OMAI formula endpoints and exact Lean proof source for local theorems with no Physlib physics counterpart. Hash and compiled-name checks detect drift and provenance errors; they are not automatic symbolic translation or numerical validation.

operators.formula_latex: t_{cure} = \int\limits_{\alpha_{0,cure}}^{\alpha_{cure}} \frac{\left(1 - \alpha'\right)^{- n_{cure}}}{A_{1,cure} e^{- \frac{E_{1,cure}}{N_{A} T k_{B}}} + A_{2,cure} \alpha'^{m_{cure}} e^{- \frac{E_{2,cure}}{N_{A} T k_{B}}}}\, d\alpha'

interpretations: kamal_cure_conversion gives the isothermal cure time t_cure from alpha_0 to alpha as the integral of 1/((1 - a)^n (k1 + k2 a^m)), with k_i = A_i exp(-E_i/(N_A k_B T)), T in kelvin and E_i per mole; the conversion alpha(t) is its inverse, shown to exist and to solve the rate law locally near every interior cure time. A_1, A_2 >= 0, m >= 0, any real n, 0 <= alpha_0, and either A_1 > 0 or alpha_0 > 0 with A_2 > 0, so that the rate is positive below full cure.

Conversion is a fraction in [0, 1], not a percentage. The rate law is the single-(1 - alpha)^n Kamal-Sourour form at constant temperature, without diffusion control, a temperature-dependent maximum conversion or separate exponents on the two terms; isothermal values are meaningful only while T_g(alpha(t)) stays below the cure temperature.

dibenedetto_glass_transition reads the conversion alpha in [0, 1] and the parameters T_g0 (uncured), T_ginf (fully cured) and lambda > 0, in the Pascault-Williams form, with temperatures in kelvin as the GlassTransitionTemperature node stores them. T_g(alpha) is taken as independent of cure path and specific to one stoichiometry. lambda is commonly identified with Delta C_p,inf / Delta C_p,0; that identification is not proved here.
